title: Class prevalence changes which chest radiograph dataset looks better: a cross-dataset audit of four publicly released classifiers

description:
Analysis code and derived results accompanying a manuscript submitted to BMC Medical Imaging.

The study audits four publicly released chest radiograph classifiers (identical architecture, differing pretraining source) on three independently collected datasets (NIH ChestX-ray14, Kermany, VinDr-CXR), each reduced to one identically defined binary task. It reports that resampling all cohorts to a common class prevalence contracted the calibration spread in seven of eight model-label combinations and reversed the calibration ranking in all eight, and it establishes the reference quantity against which such reversals must be judged: under a null of identical calibration across datasets, prior matching alone reorders them in 82.5-84.4% of replicates. The analytic expectation for three exchangeable datasets is 1 - 1/3! = 83.33%. The package also includes a corrected implementation of the variance estimator of DeLong's test and verification scripts that re-derive every reported number from the authoritative result files.

Data and pretrained weights are not included; see the repository README for their original sources and terms of use.
